definition: Logistics engineering designs and evaluates systems for moving, storing and supplying goods or materials.
example: An engineer redesigns a warehouse layout to shorten replenishment routes.

definition: A lookup table stores preassigned results so an input can retrieve an answer without recomputing it.
example: An embedded controller maps sensor readings to calibrated temperatures using a lookup table.

definition: Machining technology concerns equipment, tooling and methods for shaping workpieces by removing material.
example: A machinist chooses a milling process to produce an accurately sized slot.

definition: Mainframe storage comprises the hardware and software used to retain, organize and access data for mainframe workloads.
example: A bank allocates disk volumes to handle its overnight batch processing.

definition: Margin lending allows a borrower to borrow against securities held as collateral, subject to collateral requirements.
example: A brokerage requires more collateral after the market value of a pledged account falls.

definition: Market capitalization is the market price per share multiplied by the number of shares outstanding.
example: An analyst calculates a company’s market capitalization using its closing share price.

definition: Market depth describes how much buying and selling interest is available at different prices near the market price.
example: A trader inspects the order book to see whether a large order would consume several price levels.

definition: Mass media are channels and organizations that distribute content to large audiences.
example: A radio station broadcasts a weather update to listeners across a region.

definition: Master production records specify the standard ingredients, instructions and controls for making a defined product or batch.
example: A quality team checks a completed batch record against the approved master production record.

definition: Material flow is the movement of physical materials through storage, processing and distribution operations.
example: A factory maps how parts move between receiving, assembly and shipping.

definition: A mechanic's lien is a statutory claim against property that can secure payment for qualifying work or materials supplied to improve it.
example: A contractor asks whether unpaid renovation work qualifies for a lien.
sense_note: Requirements and terminology vary by jurisdiction.

definition: Mechanical drawings communicate the geometry, dimensions and other requirements of parts, assemblies or mechanical installations.
example: A fabricator uses a drawing to check the diameter and location of mounting holes.

definition: Mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems are coordinated building services that supply functions such as climate control, power, water and drainage.
example: A design team checks that ductwork and electrical conduits do not interfere above a ceiling.

definition: Media ethics concerns principles for making responsible decisions about gathering, creating and distributing content.
example: An editor weighs the public interest against a private person's privacy before publishing a photograph.

definition: Medical devices are instruments, equipment, implants or software intended for a medical purpose such as diagnosis, monitoring or treatment.
example: A clinic uses a pulse oximeter to measure a patient's blood oxygen saturation.
sense_note: Formal regulatory definitions vary by jurisdiction.

definition: Medical equipment comprises physical apparatus used in clinical care, diagnosis, monitoring or treatment.
example: A clinic maintains its examination tables and patient monitors as part of its equipment inventory.

definition: A meta tag is an HTML element that provides information or instructions about a document without adding visible page content.
example: A web developer sets a viewport meta tag to help a page display properly on phones.

definition: The metaverse is a broad concept for persistent, shared digital spaces where people interact, often through avatars.
example: A virtual exhibition lets attendees walk through the same digital gallery and speak to one another.
sense_note: The label has no single settled technical definition.

definition: The metric system is a decimal system of measurement built around units such as the metre and gram.
example: A designer converts millimetres to metres by dividing the measurement by 1,000.

definition: Microcontrollers are integrated circuits that combine a processor, memory and input-output interfaces for embedded control.
example: A washing machine uses a microcontroller to read the door switch and coordinate the wash cycle.

definition: Microscopic anatomy studies tissue and cellular structures too small to examine in detail without magnification.
example: A student distinguishes skeletal muscle from connective tissue on a microscope slide.

definition: A microsite is a small website or distinct section created around a narrow purpose, campaign or topic.
example: A museum builds a microsite with event details and registration for a special exhibit.

definition: MicroStrategy metrics are calculation objects that define how data is aggregated or otherwise computed in MicroStrategy reports and dashboards.
example: A dashboard uses a reusable metric to compute net sales by region.

definition: A mill test report documents the tested chemical composition and mechanical properties of a manufactured material lot, typically metal.
example: A receiving inspector compares a steel heat number with the corresponding report before accepting delivery.

definition: Millimeter waves are electromagnetic waves with wavelengths of about one to ten millimetres.
example: A short-range radar uses millimeter waves to measure object distance.

definition: Mineralogy studies minerals, including their chemistry, structure, physical properties and formation.
example: A geologist distinguishes two similar minerals by comparing hardness and crystal form.

definition: Mixed reality combines digital content with a view of the physical surroundings so that virtual objects can be positioned in, and may respond to, the real environment.
example: A maintenance trainee views a digital alignment marker anchored to a physical pump.
sense_note: The boundary between mixed and augmented reality varies across sources.

definition: Mobile computing uses portable devices to run applications and access information away from a fixed workstation.
example: A field technician updates a maintenance record from a tablet on site.

definition: Models for life contingencies use probabilities and cash-flow timing to value payments that depend on events such as survival or death.
example: An actuary estimates the present value of payments from a lifetime annuity.

definition: Molecular engineering designs materials or systems by controlling their structures and interactions at the molecular scale.
example: A materials researcher designs polymer chains to alter how a coating repels water.

definition: Motor control firmware is low-level code running within a motor controller to manage its sensors, timing and output signals.
example: An embedded controller adjusts its drive output when feedback shows the motor slowing.

definition: Motor control software comprises programs and algorithms for commanding and monitoring a motor’s speed, position or torque.
example: A machine application requests a new motor speed and tracks whether the drive reaches it.

definition: A multi-agent system consists of multiple decision-making entities that interact in a shared environment.
example: A warehouse simulation models robots that coordinate to avoid blocking one another.

definition: A multi-core processor integrates multiple processing cores that can execute work concurrently.
example: A video editor distributes independent rendering tasks across several cores.

definition: Multi-core symmetric multiprocessing allows a common operating system to schedule work across peer processor cores that share main memory.
example: An operating system runs separate application threads on different cores while both access shared buffers.

definition: Multi-core software is designed to use multiple processor cores to execute portions of work concurrently.
example: A simulation assigns independent regions of a grid to separate worker threads.

definition: Multi-touch input detects and distinguishes multiple simultaneous contacts on a touch-sensitive surface.
example: A map application turns the movement of two fingers into a zoom gesture.

definition: Multicultural education uses curricula and teaching practices that recognize cultural diversity and address inequities in learning.
example: A teacher compares accounts of the same event from several cultural perspectives.

definition: Multitenancy lets separate customers share a service or infrastructure while keeping their information and configuration logically isolated.
example: A shared ticketing system restricts each organization to its own support cases.

definition: Music theory studies how elements such as pitch, rhythm, harmony and form are organized in music.
example: A student identifies the cadence that marks the end of a musical phrase.
